title: How Båstadgruppen Is Building a Reliable Product-Data Foundation for Lower-Impact Workwear
summary: Båstadgruppen partnered with Carbonfact to turn fragmented data into credible product-level insights for sustainability investments, tenders and compliance.
body_markdown:
Båstadgruppen is a Nordic B2B supplier of workwear, safety and occupational apparel and footwear.


For workwear and safety-footwear brands like Båstadgruppen, environmental data isn't just a reporting requirement. It's evidence that a product will perform under demanding conditions and hold up over years of use, the core of the durability promise these categories are built on.


At the same time, Båstadgruppen’s B2B customers increasingly expect standardized environmental data as part of tender processes. But


[standardizing product-level data](https://www.carbonfact.com/lca-for-fashion)


is complex: products combine technical fabrics, trims, protective components, and multiple suppliers, while data is often scattered across different systems and formats.


That’s why Båstadgruppen partnered with Carbonfact – to turn fragmented data into credible product-level insights it can use for directing sustainability investments, tenders, and regulatory compliance.


"Our main goal is to reduce our impact by 50% by 2030 compared to 2024. The main goal with partnering with Carbonfact is to be able to have reliable data, so that we can make data-driven, educated decisions in our strategy."


Jacob Larsson


Sustainability Specialist at Båstadgruppen


## Interview With Jacob Larsson, Båstadgruppen’s Sustainability Specialist


## The Problem: No Clear View of Where Emissions Came From


Båstadgruppen serves industries like construction, manufacturing, healthcare, and outdoor work. Rather than operating as a single consumer-facing brand, it manages multiple brands and product categories, grown in part through acquiring smaller companies.


Product and supplier information was spread across PDFs, Excel files, and emails, in different formats across Båstadgruppen's brands and suppliers, some of it incomplete, outdated, or difficult to validate.


"We were not able to identify where our emissions and impacts originated. We could not tell which material or which supplier was having the highest impact, and because of that, we could not effectively prioritize our sustainability investments."


Jacob Larsson


Sustainability Specialist at Båstadgruppen


Båstadgruppen’s small sustainability and compliance team was also responsible for chemicals and regulatory topics. The company therefore needed a solution that would reduce manual work and be an extension of Båstadgruppen’s small team.


## Why Båstadgruppen Chose Carbonfact: From Unstructured Files to Usable Data


"We chose Carbonfact because of its accessibility and user-friendliness. All the important values were presented in a very intuitive way, which made it much easier to implement them in our strategic work on how to reduce our impact."


Jacob Larsson


Sustainability Specialist at Båstadgruppen


Several capabilities made Carbonfact the right fit:


-


Ability to work with imperfect data:


Båstadgruppen could upload the product and supplier information it already had, even when data was incomplete or inconsistent. The platform automatically fills data gaps using


[smart rules](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/platform/heuristics-and-rules) built from running over 50 million apparel and footwear LCAs.


-


Granular Scope 3 measurement:


Carbonfact uses more than 150,000 fashion- and region-specific emission factors to calculate emissions across materials, manufacturing processes, suppliers, and locations. This gives Båstadgruppen a detailed view of Scope 3, where most of its footprint lies. The platform also incorporates Scope 1 and 2 operational emissions into


[GHG Protocol-aligned company footprint calculations.](https://www.carbonfact.com/carbon-accounting-software-fashion)


-


Standardization:


Carbonfact helped establish one data-collection format across suppliers, articles, brands, and categories.


-


Hands-on expert support:


Carbonfact’s data team cleaned initial BOM files, analyzed data gaps, and identified missing inputs. To support the Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) for Båstadgruppen’s 239 T-shirt, its science team developed


[bespoke emission factors](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/platform/bespoke-ef) for cotton spinning, knitting, bleaching, dyeing, finishing, and garment assembly.


-


Connected ecosystem:


Carbonfact


[integrates with Retraced](https://www.carbonfact.com/integrations) , Båstadgruppen’s supply-chain traceability platform, and is building a future connection with Delogue, its product lifecycle management platform. Connecting the systems helps its small team avoid duplicate work and build a more integrated data ecosystem.


The result?


Product, BOM, and purchase-order data now feed directly into Carbonfact’s LCA calculations. Instead of manually searching through PDFs and emails, Båstadgruppen can see product-level impact breakdowns, identify hotspots, and prioritize further data collection.


“Carbonfact can fill in data gaps with heuristics and reference datasets, so we can get value from the platform without having 100% accuracy in our own data. We can implement what we have into the system, and the system automatically fills in the rest, so we can start finding hotspots and identify where to prioritize."


Jacob Larsson


Sustainability Specialist at Båstadgruppen


## What's Next: 100% LCA Coverage and Regulatory Readiness


Before working with Carbonfact, Båstadgruppen had not conducted product Life Cycle Assessments. Although free tools offered simplified calculations, the team wanted results that were credible.


"There are free tools you can use for simpler LCAs, but for it to be comparable and trustworthy, it needs to follow recognized ISO standards. We did not want to risk greenwashing. If we publish something, we want it to be trustworthy."


Jacob Larsson


Sustainability Specialist at Båstadgruppen


Workwear makes Life Cycle Assessment particularly challenging. Footprinting must account for technical garments, PPE, safety footwear, and complex combinations of trims, specialty fibers, laminates, finishes, and numerous suppliers.


Through its work with brands including Snickers Workwear and Carhartt, Carbonfact understands these category-specific complexities. With Carbonfact, Båstadgruppen can:


-


Handle complexity at the SKU level:


**** Calculate detailed footprints across colors, sizes, suppliers, and multi-component products.


-


Calculate LCAs at scale:


Once data is processed,


[Carbonfact’s LCA engine](https://www.carbonfact.com/lca-for-fashion)


automatically calculates product footprints across the full catalog, covering 16 environmental impact indicators.


-


Produce credible, auditable results:


Carbonfact's methodology follows recognized LCA standards, and its engine and procedures are


[audited annually by PwC](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/platform/carbonfact-pwc-reviewed) .


For Båstadgruppen, this enables a "


[measure once, report everywhere approach](https://www.carbonfact.com/sustainability-reporting-textile) " : the same product-level data can support customer requests, tender submissions, eco-design, EPDs, and future Digital Product Passport requirements.


EPDs are one example:


an increasingly requested, verified, and registered document that communicates a product's quantified environmental impact over its full lifecycle. Carbonfact and Båstadgruppen developed an EPD package for one product, the 239 T-shirt, which has since entered independent verification.


## What Båstadgruppen Uses Carbonfact For


- [Carbon accounting](https://www.carbonfact.com/carbon-accounting-software-fashion?__hstc=212388875.cc71eacb8a848508290072bd367162a8.1793698656791.1793698656791.1793698656791.1&__hssc=212388875.1.1793698656791&__hsfp=c321d5924fe28441e2e7b528d6167c03) : automates Scope 1, 2, and 3 GHG tracking across Båstadgruppen's brands.


- [Product LCA](https://www.carbonfact.com/lca-for-fashion)


:


SKU-level lifecycle assessments covering CO2eq and the 16 PEFCR environmental indicators.


- [ERP, PLM, and traceability connections](https://www.carbonfact.com/data-management-software)


:


data pulled directly from Båstadgruppen's existing systems, including its Retraced integration, instead of exported and re-imported by hand.


- [Decarbonization and eco-design](https://www.carbonfact.com/decarbonization)


:


product simulations, company-level reduction scenarios, multi-indicator PEF simulations, and bespoke emission factors, developed with direct access to Carbonfact's science team.


- [Digital Product Passport](https://www.carbonfact.com/digital-product-passport-software)


:


building the LCA data foundation Båstadgruppen will need as product regulatory requirements for textiles approach.


- [Heuristics and gap-filling](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/platform/data-augmentation-rules)


:


data augmentation rules that fill missing data points so the team can calculate results before its own data is complete.
